Rae (support): Hey team — Sprites Labs reported intermittent 429s + high p95 latency when sending large-context completion requests to model gptx-64k. Pattern: starts fine, then after ~90s of steady traffic a burst of 429s for ~20-40s. Any quick theories? :thinking:

Ava (support): Repro payload they sent is ~120k tokens (they're concatenating doc chunks). Headers include x-client-id and they use streaming=false. They said errors look like '429 model overloaded' (no auth error).

Diego (infra): Can you paste the raw curl (sanitized) and the X-Rate-Limit headers if present? Also which region/endpoint?

Rae (support): Sure — sanitized example:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-64k","prompt":"<~120k tokens>","stream":false}'
```
Region: us-west-2. No custom timeout on client. They get a few successful responses then 429 bursts.

Samira (mleng): This smells like per-model throughput + long-context scheduling interaction. Quick reminder of runtime behavior: for very large contexts we move to a slower execution path and per-request latency increases nonlinearly. We also enforce soft/hard per-model windows: soft RPM/TM and a short burst window where the scheduler will start rejecting when the internal queue/backpressure exceeds thresholds. For gptx-64k our current rules (hosted) are approx: RPM=600, TPM=4200, max_concurrency=6 for 64k-class requests. (smaller contexts have higher concurrency).

Diego (infra): Adding logs from infra-bot for that customer timeframe:

infra-bot: [1918003502] model=gptx-64k region=us-west-2 queue_len=12 servicing=6 inflight_nat=6 drops=3 -> 429s returned
infra-bot: [1918003518] avg_proc_ms=5400 p95=9800 memory_pressure=0.83

Samira (mleng): See those numbers — avg proc ~5.4s and p95 ~9.8s. With concurrency=6 the effective throughput is low; if the customer keeps firing requests at a higher RPM, the internal scheduler queues them. We have a short burst window (approx 30s sampling) that allows bursts to pass, but once it fills, we start rejecting to preserve SLOs for other tenants. That explains the ~20-40s bursts of 429s.

Ava (support): Ok — so it's not an auth or billing issue, it's capacity + long-context. Customer asked if there's a config flag they can toggle to avoid 429s.

Samira (mleng): Workarounds:
- Use streaming=true so tokens are flushed earlier and runtime can free KV/cache sooner (if application can handle it).
- Break the prompt into multiple shorter calls (stitch on client side) or use retrieval + summarization to reduce context size.
- Try a model variant optimized for long context but lower latency (e.g., gptx-64k-lite-quant) if available — lower per-request memory but may trade some quality.
- If consistent high throughput with large contexts is required, recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private to get reserved capacity.

Diego (infra): For support repros, ask them to run a simple loop repro with client-side pacing and show X-Rate-Limit headers. E.g. do this to reproduce locally:

```
for i in {1..30}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \ 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
    -d '{"model":"gptx-64k","prompt":"<~120k>","stream":false}' &
done
wait
```
Look at returned headers: x-rw-rpm-left, x-rw-tpm-left, x-rw-concurrency-left (example header names).

Rae (support): I asked them to run that loop and capture headers and we'll attach logs. Anything we should escalate to runtime oncall?

Samira (mleng): If they can demonstrate 1) consistent reproduce with <10s gaps and 2) queue_len spikes >10 leading to drops, then escalate. Provide the request IDs and timestamps. We'll want a flamegraph from runtime for that window.

oncall-eng-runtime: Pinged. If you can provide request_ids + region + approximate timestamps (UTC) we'll pull scheduler traces. Also note that short client-side retry loops (immediate retries on 429) will amplify the problem; ask them to apply exponential backoff (jitter).

Ava (support): Customer is doing immediate retries with no backoff — likely making it worse. I'll ask them to add jitter backoff and try streaming or smaller chunks. Also offering a trial of dedicated capacity for a week while they evaluate. :white_check_mark:

Rae (support): Action items:
- Ava: share repro loop + headers + request IDs (customer) — due EOD
- Samira: prep guidance blurb on long-context best practices for support KB
- Diego/oncall-eng-runtime: hold traces for 1918003500-1918003580 in us-west-2 for gptx-64k

Ava (support): Noted, will follow up with the customer and update thread when I have headers.

Diego (infra): FYI we'll look into whether we should surface a clearer "long-context backpressure" header in responses. Could reduce confusion.

Rae (support): Thanks all. Closing loop after customer confirms backoff + streaming test.
